title: Support Operations Analysis Report
executive_summary: Analysis of 347 support tickets reveals a total labor cost of $27,422.90 and a mean resolution time of ~75.2 minutes. Team Beta carries the highest labor cost, phone channel resolves tickets fastest, and email tickets reopen at roughly twice the rate of chat tickets. A small high-cost, low-satisfaction segment warrants targeted intervention, and moderate agent concentration suggests manageable workload distribution.

key_findings.statement: The dataset contains 347 tickets with a mean resolution time of 75.2 minutes and a total labor cost of $27,422.90.
Team Beta incurred the highest labor cost at $10,247.36, followed by Gamma at $9,387.73 and Alpha at $7,787.81. Beta's cost exceeds Alpha's by $2,459.55.
Phone channel resolves tickets fastest at 69.3 minutes on average, followed by email at 73.0 minutes and chat at 83.0 minutes. Chat is the slowest channel.
Email tickets reopen at 17.2% versus 7.8% for chat, representing an increase of ~119.8% relative to the chat reopen rate — email tickets are more than twice as likely to be reopened.
12 tickets meet the high-cost (≥$100) and low-satisfaction (score ≤2) criteria. Of these, 8.3% were reopened, indicating a small but notable at-risk segment requiring focused follow-up.

Resolution time has a median of 65.0 minutes and a standard deviation of 51.9 minutes, indicating a right-skewed distribution. Mean satisfaction among scored tickets is 4.15 out of 5, with 19 tickets missing a satisfaction score.
18 distinct agents handled the 347 tickets. The busiest single agent handled 26 tickets, representing 7.5% of total volume — a moderate concentration with no single agent dominating workload.

limitations: 19 tickets are missing satisfaction scores, which may introduce bias into the satisfaction mean if missingness is non-random (e.g., correlated with poor outcomes).
The high-cost low-satisfaction segment contains only 12 tickets; conclusions drawn from this group have limited statistical power.
Labor cost is derived from a joined roster; any agents absent from the roster or with incorrect rates would distort team-level cost comparisons.
The dataset represents a single export snapshot with no time dimension, so trends over time cannot be assessed.
Reopen rates are based on a binary flag and do not capture multiple reopenings, potentially understating chronic resolution failures.
conclusion: Support operations are broadly healthy — satisfaction averages 4.15 and the top agent handles only 7.5% of tickets — but two areas merit action: the email channel's reopen rate is ~120% higher than chat's, and Team Beta's labor cost leads all teams at $10,247. Investigating email resolution quality and Beta's cost drivers should be prioritized, alongside outreach to the 12 high-cost, low-satisfaction customers.
